key_path: Open a Zerodha trading + demat account (online KYC: PAN, Aadhaar e-sign, bank proof, in-person verification by video/selfie). Takes 1-3 days
Sign up on developers.kite.trade (separate developer account), verify email
Create an app: pick Personal (free, orders/portfolio only, no market data) or Connect (Rs 500/month per key, includes live and historical data). Paid apps need wallet credits topped up
Set the redirect URL, get api_key + api_secret
Whitelist a static IP in the app settings before any order can be placed (SEBI retail-algo framework, mandatory since 1 Apr 2026)
Every day: open kite.zerodha.com/connect/login?v=3&api_key=..., log in with Zerodha user ID, password and TOTP 2FA, then capture request_token from the redirect
POST /session/token with checksum SHA-256(api_key+request_token+api_secret) to get the access_token. It expires at 6 AM the next day
human_gates_notes: KYC comes from opening a SEBI-regulated broking account. 'credit_card_required' here means a prepaid wallet top-up for the paid Connect tier; the Personal tier is free. Daily login with TOTP cannot be automated within the ToS. A static IP whitelist is required for orders.

agent_native_auth.cli_login: no. No official CLI. The login is a browser redirect flow that runs daily
agent_native_auth.oauth_dcr_for_mcp: no. The hosted MCP (mcp.kite.trade) does not advertise MCP OAuth (/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns 404). Instead it exposes a `login` tool that returns a Kite login URL for the human to open
agent_native_auth.scoped_keys: partial. Personal vs Connect app types. The self-hosted MCP supports an EXCLUDED_TOOLS env var to make a read-only instance
agent_native_auth.sandbox_test_credentials: no. There is no paper-trading sandbox; every call hits the live account
agent_native_auth.free_tier: yes. The Personal API is free (since Mar 2025) but has no market data

remote.auth: No API key needed. A session-level `login` tool returns a Kite login URL and the user logs in with Zerodha credentials + TOTP. Not MCP-spec OAuth

mcp.local: github.com/zerodha/kite-mcp-server (Go; stdio/HTTP/SSE; needs your own KITE_API_KEY/SECRET)
mcp.tools_observed: 22 tools incl. place_order, modify_order, cancel_order, place_gtt_order, get_holdings, get_quotes, get_historical_data, login (probed unauthenticated tools/list 2026-10-11)
mcp.one_click_install: no. README uses `npx mcp-remote https://mcp.kite.trade/mcp` in claude_desktop_config.json. Also listed in third-party directories

docs_for_agents.openapi: no official OpenAPI spec. Docs are HTML at kite.trade/docs/connect/v3/

score_justification: The hosted MCP is excellent for an existing Zerodha user: no key, one URL, full trading tools. But the regulated KYC account, daily TOTP re-login and static-IP rule mean an agent can never run unattended.
best_practice: A zero-config hosted MCP that sidesteps API-key provisioning entirely by asking the end user to log in through a tool call
biggest_gap: The daily access-token expiry at 6 AM with mandatory 2FA, plus no llms.txt/OpenAPI and no sandbox. Agents trade against real money with no test mode
